body.claim: Ordinals shift when a declaration is inserted ahead, and the cardinality equality check in by_symbol_and_path is the only thing that stops that from repointing an anchor.
body.detail: Inserting a second same-name same-kind declaration takes the count from N to N+1, and the rung refuses outright when the count is not exactly what was recorded, so the anchor falls through rather than resolving to the neighbour that inherited its ordinal. Relax that to a range or a minimum and ordinals become silently wrong, which is the failure I2 forbids. The residual case the check cannot see is an edit that removes one declaration and adds another ahead of the target at once: the count is unchanged and only the node path descent and the node kind comparison stand between that and a false reattachment. Supersedes an earlier record of mine that claimed the shift repoints anchors on its own; it does not, because of this check.
